## Pros and Cons

- **Excellent value** — Starter plan at €2.49/mo is cheaper than NordVPN, ExpressVPN, and ProtonVPN's equivalent tiers

- **WireGuard + OpenVPN + Dausos** — Modern protocol support includes the fast WireGuard protocol and their own in-house Dausos protocol

## Surfshark Review 2026: The Full Breakdown

The VPN market in 2026 is more crowded than ever. NordVPN dominates headlines, ExpressVPN markets to power users, ProtonVPN targets privacy purists, and a dozen others fight for scraps. Amid this competitive landscape, Surfshark has quietly built one of the most compelling all-around VPN services — one that doesn't force you to choose between value and quality.

After putting Surfshark through weeks of real-world testing — speed benchmarks across six global locations, streaming tests on Netflix, Hulu, Disney+, BBC iPlayer, and Amazon Prime, privacy leak tests, customer support interactions, and feature-by-feature comparisons — we're ready to deliver our definitive take. Here's the full picture.

---

### 1. Speed and Performance: Good, Not Great — But Good Enough

Speed is where Surfshark shows both its strength and its ceiling. We ran benchmarks using the WireGuard protocol across servers in the US (New York), UK (London), Germany (Frankfurt), Japan (Tokyo), Australia (Sydney), and Brazil (São Paulo), connecting from a 500 Mbps fiber connection.

**WireGuard download speeds:**

| Location | Avg Download (Mbps) | Latency (ms) |
|---|---|---|
| US (New York) | 285 | 38 |
| UK (London) | 268 | 42 |
| Germany (Frankfurt) | 259 | 44 |
| Japan (Tokyo) | 178 | 162 |
| Australia (Sydney) | 145 | 238 |
| Brazil (São Paulo) | 166 | 195 |

With WireGuard, Surfshark delivers about 85-90% of our base speed on nearby servers and roughly 50-65% on far-flung ones. That's respectable — fast enough for 4K streaming, large downloads, and gaming — but not class-leading. For comparison, ExpressVPN's Lightway protocol delivers around 310 Mbps on the same US server, and NordVPN's NordLynx hits 320 Mbps.

Where Surfshark falls short noticeably is on its OpenVPN connections. OpenVPN speeds averaged around 120-140 Mbps on the US server — about half of WireGuard speeds. If speed matters to you, stick with WireGuard (which you should be using anyway on any modern VPN).

The real story here is that Surfshark's speeds are more than adequate for 99% of real-world use cases. The difference between 285 Mbps and 320 Mbps is invisible in practice — both can stream 4K on multiple devices simultaneously. Surfshark's "good enough" performance is a fair trade-off for its drastically lower price.

---

### 2. Security and Privacy: Where Surfshark Shines

This is Surfshark's strongest category, and it's not close.

**Encryption:** Surfshark uses AES-256-GCM (the gold standard) for OpenVPN and IKEv2, and ChaCha20-Poly1305 for WireGuard. Their in-house Dausos protocol adds AEGIS-256X2 encryption — essentially military-grade protection across every connection type.

**No-logs policy:** Surfshark has been audited by Deloitte — one of the Big Four accounting firms — in 2023 and again in 2025. Both audits confirmed that Surfshark adheres to its strict no-logs commitments. This gives Surfshark a level of third-party verification that few VPNs can match (ExpressVPN has PwC audits, NordVPN and ProtonVPN have Deloitte audits — the top tier is surprisingly small).

**RAM-only servers:** Every Surfshark server runs entirely on volatile memory (RAM). When a server is rebooted, everything on it is wiped clean. This means no data can persist on a server if it's seized or compromised. Not all VPNs do this — many still use SSDs that potentially store data between sessions.

**Security audits:** The track record is impressive:
- Cure53 (2026) — Infrastructure and Dausos protocol audit
- SecuRing (2025) — Infrastructure security assessment
- Cure53 (2021) — Infrastructure review, no significant concerns found
- Cure53 (2018) — Browser extension audit, robust security confirmed

**Bug bounty:** Surfshark runs an active bug bounty program on HackerOne, encouraging researchers to find and report vulnerabilities. This is a mature security practice that not all VPNs — even premium ones — maintain consistently.

**MultiHop (Double VPN):** Surfshark calls its double VPN feature "MultiHop." You can chain traffic through two different countries, with each hop adding another layer of encryption. This is useful for journalists, activists, or anyone with above-average threat models. The dynamic MultiHop (Nexus feature) lets you pick specific entry and exit points.

**NoBorders mode:** When you're traveling to countries with heavy internet censorship (China, UAE, Russia), NoBorders automatically detects network restrictions and connects you to the most effective server for bypassing them. In our tests, NoBorders worked reliably from a simulated restricted network.

---

### 3. Server Network: 3,200+ Servers in 100 Countries

Surfshark's network has grown steadily and now spans 3,200+ servers in 100 countries. That's a strong footprint — fewer servers than NordVPN's 6,000+ but more countries covered than ExpressVPN (94) and ProtonVPN (90+).

Server distribution is weighted toward high-demand regions:
- **North America:** 800+ servers (US has the most, with servers in 25+ US cities)
- **Europe:** 1,200+ servers (London, Amsterdam, Frankfurt are the busiest)
- **Asia-Pacific:** 500+ servers (Tokyo, Singapore, Sydney, Mumbai)
- **South America:** 300+ servers (São Paulo, Buenos Aires, Santiago)
- **Middle East & Africa:** 200+ servers (Dubai, Istanbul, Tel Aviv, Johannesburg)

All servers support P2P traffic, and Surfshark clearly labels which servers are optimized for streaming. Dedicated IP servers are available as an add-on (see pricing section), and Static IP servers are available in select locations.

The network uses virtual server locations (servers physically located in one country but assigned an IP from another) in regions where physical infrastructure is limited. Surfshark is transparent about this — you can check which locations are virtual on their server list page.

---

### 5. Streaming and Content Unblocking

Surfshark markets itself as a streaming-friendly VPN, and for the most part, it delivers.

**Netflix:** US Netflix works reliably on US servers. We tested Netflix libraries from the US, UK, Canada, Japan, and Germany — all worked on the first try. Netflix's VPN detection has become more aggressive in 2026, and Surfshark holds up well against it, though not as seamlessly as NordVPN's dedicated streaming IPs.

**Disney+:** Disney+ is notoriously aggressive about blocking VPNs. Surfshark worked on US Disney+ about 70% of the time in our tests. When it failed, switching to a different US server usually resolved the issue within 30 seconds.

**BBC iPlayer:** This was the most hit-or-miss. On some days, iPlayer recognized our IP as a VPN and blocked content. Switching between London servers resolved it roughly 80% of the time. Notably, ExpressVPN and NordVPN had 95%+ success rates on the same tests.

**HBO Max / Amazon Prime Video:** Both worked consistently across multiple testing sessions.

**Hulu:** Worked without issues on US servers.

For casual streaming of Netflix and Amazon Prime, Surfshark is great. For heavy streaming of region-locked content like BBC iPlayer, you may occasionally need to switch servers. If streaming is your primary VPN use case, NordVPN or ExpressVPN are slightly more reliable — but Surfshark is still very capable.

---

### 6. Apps and User Experience

Surfshark's apps are clean, intuitive, and available on every major platform:

- **Windows, macOS, Linux** — Full desktop apps with all features
- **iOS, Android** — Mobile apps with GPS Override (Android) and kill switch
- **Browser extensions** — Chrome, Firefox, Edge
- **TV platforms** — Fire TV, Apple TV
- **Router** — Manual setup guide, or flash with compatible firmware

**Windows app highlights:** The Windows client is well-designed. It shows server load percentages, has a favorites system for frequently used servers, and includes the full feature set (CleanWeb, MultiHop, Bypasser/split tunneling, Kill Switch, Rotating IP). Connection times with WireGuard average under 3 seconds.

**Mobile apps:** Both iOS and Android apps are polished and functional. The Android app includes GPS Override (match your GPS to your VPN location), and both apps support the full CleanWeb suite. The mobile apps have a slightly simpler UI than desktop, with fewer customization options, but they cover the essentials well.

**Bypasser (split tunneling):** This feature lets you choose which apps bypass the VPN tunnel. It's useful for banking apps that don't work well with VPNs or local streaming services. Available on Windows, Mac, and Android. iOS doesn't support split tunneling (an Apple limitation, not Surfshark's fault).

**Linux app:** The Linux app is command-line based, which will delight power users but may frustrate beginners. It supports WireGuard and OpenVPN connections and includes CleanWeb and Kill Switch, but doesn't have the full Nexus feature set.

---

### 7. Customer Support

Surfshark's customer support is consistently rated as one of the best in the industry.

**Live chat:** Available 24/7. We tested five times at different hours and never waited more than 45 seconds for an initial response. Agents were knowledgeable, didn't use scripts, and resolved our issues (a connection problem on Linux, a question about Dedicated IP setup) professionally.

**Email/tickets:** Responses averaged 2-4 hours for standard requests. Detailed, personalized answers from the same team that handles live chat.

**Help center:** A comprehensive knowledge base with setup guides, troubleshooting articles, and FAQs organized by topic and platform.

**Phone:** Available during business hours, European time zone. We tested once and got through in 3 minutes. The agent was helpful but couldn't do anything the live chat team couldn't.

Surfshark's support is genuinely good — not just "good for a budget VPN." The live chat team resolves most issues on the first contact, which is the mark of a well-trained support organization.

### 9. Who Should Use Surfshark?

**Surfshark is ideal for:**

- **Families and multi-device households** — The unlimited device policy is the killer feature. One subscription secures every phone, laptop, tablet, and smart TV in your home
- **Budget-conscious users** — At €2.49/mo on the long-term plan, Surfshark dramatically undercuts premium competitors while delivering comparable security
- **Streamers (casual)** — Netflix, Amazon Prime, and Hulu work reliably. If you mostly watch US content, Surfshark is more than adequate
- **Privacy-minded users** — Deloitte-audited no-logs policy, RAM-only servers, and regular Cure53 penetration tests make Surfshark a legitimate privacy tool
- **Travelers** — NoBorders mode and obfuscated servers help bypass censorship in countries with internet restrictions

**Surfshark is less ideal for:**

- **Streaming power users** — If you need guaranteed access to BBC iPlayer, Disney+, and niche regional libraries 100% of the time without ever switching servers, ExpressVPN or NordVPN are the safer choice
- **Speed-obsessed users** — If you need every last Mbps of your gigabit connection through a VPN, NordVPN's NordLynx or ExpressVPN's Lightway will outperform WireGuard on Surfshark
- **Business/enterprise use** — Surfshark doesn't offer a dedicated business tier with centralized management. NordVPN Teams or Perimeter 81 are better choices
- **Users who need phone support** — Live chat is excellent, but phone is limited hours. If you want to be able to call at 3 AM, look elsewhere

---

### 10. The Nexus Technology: What Makes Surfshark Different

Surfshark's Nexus technology is a network-level feature set that differentiates it from most competitors:

**Rotating IP:** Your IP address changes every 5-10 minutes without dropping the VPN connection. This makes it extremely difficult for websites and trackers to build a profile of your browsing habits.

**Dynamic MultiHop:** While traditional MultiHop requires you to pick two specific countries, Nexus's Dynamic MultiHop intelligently routes your traffic through optimal nodes for both security and speed.

**GPS Override (Android):** Your GPS location matches your VPN server location, preventing apps that use GPS data from leaking your real location. This is an Android-specific feature (iOS doesn't allow GPS override) and it works well in our testing.

**Everlink:** A patented self-healing technology that instantly restores dropped VPN connections. If your VPN connection fails, Everlink re-establishes the tunnel without you noticing — no data leaks, no manual reconnection.

Nexus is the kind of innovation that genuinely improves the VPN experience, rather than being a marketing gimmick. The Rotating IP feature alone is useful for preventing tracking without requiring manual server switching.

---

### 11. Ethical and Transparency Practices

Surfshark scores well on transparency:

- **Annual transparency reports** — Published on their trust center, detailing government data requests and how they respond
- **Public trust center** — All audit reports, certifications, and security information in one place
- **VPN Trust Initiative member** — Committed to industry standards for security, advertising, and transparency
- **Supports non-profits** — Donates to Amnesty International, Internet Society, EDRi, Access Now, and the International Press Institute
- **Bug bounty program** — Active on HackerOne for responsible disclosure

This level of transparency is becoming the new standard in the VPN industry, but Surfshark was an early adopter and remains one of the most transparent services in its price class.

---

### 12. Setup and Installation

Getting started with Surfshark is straightforward:

1. Choose a plan on the Surfshark website
2. Create an account with email and password
3. Download the app for your platform (Windows, Mac, iOS, Android, or Linux)
4. Log in and click Quick-Connect
5. Done — you're protected

The entire process takes less than 5 minutes. The Quick-Connect feature selects the fastest server based on your location, which is a good default. From there, you can browse the server list, add favorites, configure CleanWeb, set up MultiHop, or enable the Kill Switch.

For router setup, Surfshark provides detailed guides for DD-WRT, AsusWRT, and pfSense. This is more involved than app setup but lets you protect every device on your network without installing anything on individual devices.

---

### 13. Refund Policy

Surfshark's 30-day money-back guarantee is straightforward:

- Full refund for any reason within 30 days of purchase
- Refund processed within 5-10 business days
- Money-back applies to all plans (monthly, annual, biennial)
- Exception: Dedicated IP add-on fees are non-refundable after 7 days

We tested the refund process by requesting one for a test account. The live chat agent confirmed our refund eligibility, and the funds appeared in our account within 4 business days. No obstacles, no retention tactics — just a clean, professional process.

---

## Final Verdict

Surfshark has earned its place in the top tier of consumer VPNs by doing something deceptively difficult: delivering genuine security, privacy, and usability at a price that doesn't feel exploitative. The unlimited device policy alone makes it the best choice for households, and the Deloitte-audited no-logs policy provides real privacy assurance.

Is it the fastest VPN? No. ExpressVPN and NordVPN beat it on raw speed. Is it the best for streaming? Only if you're watching US content — international libraries are occasionally hit-or-miss. But is it the best **value** VPN in 2026? Absolutely.

For the typical user who wants to protect their privacy, stream Netflix without geo-blocks, and secure every device in their home without paying per-device, Surfshark doesn't just compete — it leads. The combination of unlimited connections, verified no-logs policy, modern protocol support (WireGuard + Dausos), and aggressive pricing creates a package that's hard to beat.

If you have a specific need for maximum speed or guaranteed international streaming access, the extra cost of NordVPN or ExpressVPN may be justified. But for everyone else — which is most people — Surfshark delivers everything you need and nothing you don't.
